newsitem.title: GERMANY: Ruhrkohle says coal deal can avoid layoffs.
newsitem.headline: Ruhrkohle says coal deal can avoid layoffs.

text.p: Germany's main hard-coal producer, Ruhrkohle AG said the subsidy deal reached between Chancellor Helmut Kohl and mining union leaders on Thursday can be accomplished without mass layoffs.
But four of Germany's 18 coal pits are likely to be closed by the year 2000, the company said in a statement.

The Emschermulde mine, including its Ewald and Hugo pits, is already due to be closed this year. But a further three to four mines will have to be closed under the deal to curtail subsidies, Ruhrkohle said.

The mining company said the federal government would pay 2.75 billion marks in annual subsidies through the year 2000. The state government of North Rhine-Westphalia will pay one billion marks annually from 1998 to 2005.
Ruhrkohle itself will pay 200 million marks a year starting in 2001.
